answer: Computational proof-of-work per identity deters Sybil attacks by forcing every agent to solve a memory-hard puzzle tied to its key each epoch. Each operator deploys a pearl miner binary on an ocean compute node and commits a vertex proof header before joining consensus. Maintaining 1,000 fake accounts demands 4,000 GPU-hours and $1,200 in power per epoch, ensuring linear cost growth exceeds attack profit.
